question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $49u+20v=\text{gcd}(49,20).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}49 & = & 20\cdot 2 & + & 9 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 20 & = & 9\cdot 2 & + & 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 9 & = & 2\cdot 4 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(49,20)=1.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & =49-20\cdot 2 \\ 2 & =20-9\cdot 2 \\ 1 & =9-2\cdot 4.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =9-2\cdot 4 \\  & =9-[20-9\cdot 2]\cdot 4 \\  & =9\cdot 9-20\cdot 4 \\  & =[49-20\cdot 2]\cdot 9-20\cdot 4 \\  & =49\cdot 9-20\cdot 22 \\  & =49\cdot 9+20\cdot (-22)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=9$ and $v=-22.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=9+(-22)=-13.
$$
